summary: Daggett Hill steel lookout in Mackinac County, 120 ft in 1938; a 1966 report says it was being dismantled for Missouri, which no other source confirms.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with an observation room at the top
facts.status_note: A 1966 newspaper reported it was being dismantled. No source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: A newspaper described the Daggett Hill tower as the latest model, 120 feet high, with a stairway and hand rails.
A towerman at the Daggett tower near East Lake died suddenly in June 1939.
Aerial fire detection replaced three Mackinac County towers, Moran, Maple Hill and Daggett. The same report kept Moran and Maple Hill for emergency detection.
The Evening News reported the Daggett tower was being dismantled for re-erection in Missouri. No other source found confirms the Missouri site.

notes_for_editor: Brief status was unknown. The 1966 Evening News report says the tower was being dismantled for Missouri, which shows removal under way, not a confirmed current state, so facts.status is left out and status_note carries the caveat. The Missouri re-erection rests only on that one 1966 report: a WebSearch for a Missouri tower of this name found nothing. Mapcarta lists a point named Daggett Lookout Tower (type Tower, with coordinates); it may be a map label rather than a standing structure. The 1938 article is the earliest source; no build date was found. Access is not in any source. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the 1938 wording was reworded, the view is attributed to Ranger DeGraff (not the writer), the towerman entry no longer says on duty, the Mapcarta entry is described as having no dates or history, and the 1966 report's retention of Moran and Maple Hill is now stated.
